summary: Any position can contain the only value not repeated three times, so an exact solution must read all n entries in the worst case. The two-mask state machine matches that lower bound.

optimality.argument: Suppose an algorithm leaves some position unread. The other n - 1 positions can consist entirely of valid triples, while the unread position can contain either of two different singleton values. Both completed arrays satisfy the frequency promise and agree on every inspected position, yet their answers differ. Therefore every position must be inspected in the worst case, giving Omega(n). The current state machine performs constant bitwise work per entry, giving O(n) time.

replacement_checks.evidence: Changing an unread singleton position changes the required answer while leaving every inspected triple unchanged.
The implementation visits every value once and performs a constant number of bitwise operations on two integer masks.

The source-fidelity-verified examples cover one repeated value, multiple repeated values, and zero; black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary check without inspecting its definition.
